# Threat model

Last updated 2026-10-05. Status: **M** = mitigated and tested locally, **L** = mitigated and locally
verified (the feature matrix's status; tests against real PostgreSQL, and browsers where stated),
**P** = partially mitigated, **D** = designed (not yet built), **A** = accepted risk (documented).

## Assets

Customer conversations and contact data (per company); WhatsApp business tokens; payment references
and wallet balances; identity credentials and sessions; audit trails; platform administration power.

## Actors

Anonymous internet user · authenticated user of company A attacking company B · malicious or
compromised company member · compromised company owner account · malicious WhatsApp end user
(sends crafted messages/media) · forged provider (fake webhooks) · platform staff (insider) ·
supply-chain attacker · attacker with stolen database backup or read access.

## Trust boundaries

Browser ↔ web · Meta/Razorpay/Shopify/WooCommerce ↔ webhook endpoints · web/worker ↔ PostgreSQL
(roles, RLS) · worker ↔ external APIs (egress) · platform area ↔ tenant area · secret manager ↔
processes.

| T9   | **Billing fraud** (fake payment success, double credit, chargeback abuse, runaway auto-recharge)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Credit only from a captured payment fetched from Razorpay after the Checkout signature is checked against our stored order id; `billing_credit_topup` locks the top-up and checks order, amount and currency, so duplicate or reordered webhooks credit once; unique receipts/order/payment references; append-only ledger balanced at commit and unwritable by runtime roles; one active auto-recharge attempt (advisory lock + partial unique index); caps count in-flight attempts; write-ahead unknown states reconciled with Razorpay before any retry; cooldown and suspension after repeated declines; refunds/chargebacks posted from verified webhooks and may make credit negative (blocks spending). Adding a card and turning automatic top-ups on or changing them need a sign-in within the last 15 minutes (ADR-056), so a stolen session cannot raise automatic charges. | T10  | **SSRF** through webhooks, HTTP automation nodes, imports, agent endpoints                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Central egress client (`packages/core/src/egress.ts`, ADR-042): https only, port 443 or 1024+, no URL credentials; the name is resolved once, within the request deadline and with at most two system lookups in progress, and every answer checked (private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT, multicast, reserved, documentation, metadata and their IPv6 forms), then the socket connects only to the checked addresses, tried in turn (no rebinding); IP literals in any notation are checked; redirects are never followed; no shared connection pool; 64 KiB request, 256 KiB response, 10 s; framing/proxy headers and line breaks refused; per-company domain allowlist re-checked when each call is made. Loopback/http only for test targets, refused outside APP_ENV=local\|test. The automation HTTP step (P4-02) is the only surface that calls company-chosen addresses so far; outgoing webhooks and imports must use the same client. Tested: `egress.test.ts`, `automation-http.test.ts`, e2e `web-requests.spec.ts`. A network egress policy denying private ranges is still recommended as a second layer. ## Review cadence

Update this document with every phase gate. An external independent security review is required
before handling real customer data (see `docs/RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md`).
